# Story 16 — Ticket Communication & Activity (Story: CRM-96)

## Prerequisites

- Story CRM-94 (Ticket base CRUD, statuses) completed — endpoints in `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketEndpoints.cs`, DbContext in `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketDbContext.cs`.
- Story CRM-95 (Ticket assignment, priority, initial history) completed — see migration `20260825091919_AddTicketAssignmentAndHistory.cs` and `TicketHistoryEntry.cs`.
- Reuse the customer-side attachments pattern established under `backend/CRM.Api/Customers/Attachments/` (`IFileStorage`, `LocalFileStorage`, `AttachmentsOptions`, `CustomerAttachmentEndpoints.cs`).
- Reuse the notes pattern established in `backend/CRM.Api/Customers/CustomerNoteEndpoints.cs` and `frontend/CRM.Web/src/modules/customers/components/CustomerNotesSection.vue`.
- Coordinate with the Auth owner: escalation actions must be gated by roles defined in `backend/CRM.Api/Auth/Roles.cs`.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver one consolidated Ticket Communication & Activity feature that covers, in a single implementation:

1. **Ticket Conversation & Messages** (TKT-008) — threaded messages on a ticket (internal note vs. public reply) authored by agents, listed newest-first in the ticket details view.
2. **Ticket History** (TKT-009) — expose the existing `TicketHistoryEntry` timeline in the UI and extend it to record message/attachment/escalation events in addition to the status/assignment/priority events already written by `TicketEndpoints.cs`.
3. **Ticket Attachments** (TKT-010) — upload/list/download/delete files against a ticket, reusing `IFileStorage`/`LocalFileStorage`.
4. **Ticket Escalation** (TKT-011) — an explicit "escalate" action on a ticket that raises priority (per `TicketStatusRules`/priority rules from CRM-95) and records an `Escalated` history entry with reason.

**Out of scope:** SLA timers, automatic escalation, email/notification dispatch, customer-portal-authored messages, message editing/reactions. AI features (summaries, sentiment) are not part of this story.

### 4 — Endpoints

**Create file:** `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketMessageEndpoints.cs` — pattern taken from `CustomerNoteEndpoints.cs`.

Routes (all under `/api/tickets/{ticketId:guid}/messages`):

- `GET` → paginated list, newest first. Query params `page`, `pageSize`. Returns `TicketMessageDto` (id, authorUserId, authorDisplayName, body, isInternal, createdAt).
- `POST` → create. Body `CreateTicketMessageRequest { string Body; bool IsInternal }`. Author fields come from `HttpContext.User`. Reject body length > 5000 chars and empty/whitespace. On success write a `TicketHistoryEntry` with kind `MessageAdded` and `Details = { messageId, isInternal }` (JSON).
- All routes `[Authorize]`; only agents/managers/admins.

**Create file:** `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketAttachmentEndpoints.cs` — pattern taken from `CustomerAttachmentEndpoints.cs`.

Routes (under `/api/tickets/{ticketId:guid}/attachments`):

- `GET` → list.
- `POST` (multipart) → upload; reuse the same size cap and content-type allow-list constants used in `CustomerAttachmentEndpoints.cs`. On success write history entry `AttachmentAdded`.
- `GET /{attachmentId}/download` → stream via `IFileStorage`.
- `DELETE /{attachmentId}` → remove blob + row + history entry `AttachmentRemoved`. Restrict to uploader or elevated role.

**Edit file:** `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketEndpoints.cs`

- Add `POST /api/tickets/{id:guid}/escalate` accepting `EscalateTicketRequest { string Reason }` (required, ≤ 500 chars).
  - Reject when `TicketStatusRules` says the ticket is terminal (closed/resolved), returning `400` with a clear message.
  - Bump priority by one step using the priority ordering established in CRM-95 (find the priority helper in `TicketEndpoints.cs` or `TicketStatusRules.cs`; **do not** duplicate that logic).
  - Write a history entry with kind `Escalated` and details `{ reason, fromPriority, toPriority }`.
  - `[Authorize(Roles = ...)]` — limit to Manager/Admin per `Roles.cs`.
- Add `GET /api/tickets/{id:guid}/history` if it does not already exist. Verify by grepping for `history` inside `TicketEndpoints.cs`; if present, only extend the projected DTO to include new event kinds, do not add a second endpoint.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty/whitespace message body** — reject with 400 in `TicketMessageEndpoints`, and disable the submit button in `TicketMessagesSection.vue`.
- **Message length > 5000 chars** — 400 on backend, client-side counter warns at 4800.
- **Attachment exceeds size cap** — return the same error shape as `CustomerAttachmentEndpoints.cs` uses today; assert in tests.
- **Disallowed MIME type** — reuse the customer allow-list; do not silently accept.
- **Escalation on terminal ticket** — 400 "Cannot escalate a closed/resolved ticket." Enforced in `TicketEndpoints.cs` using `TicketStatusRules`.
- **Escalation at max priority** — 400 "Ticket is already at the highest priority."
- **Concurrent escalation** — two clicks may race; the second call must observe the new priority and either bump again (if still below max) or return the max-priority 400. Wrap in a single `SaveChangesAsync` per request; do not add a transaction unless the priority helper already uses one.
- **Delete attachment race** — if the blob is missing on disk but the row exists, delete the row and log a warning (match `LocalFileStorage` behaviour).
- **Non-agent user** — 403 for message create, attachment upload/delete, and escalate. Enforced by `[Authorize(Roles = …)]`.
- **Unicode in message body / filename** — verify persistence and echo round-trip preserves emoji and RTL text (Arabic already used in i18n).
- **Half-applied migration** — see § Migration / Rollback.

## Migration / Rollback

- The new migration only **adds** tables; a rollback is `dotnet ef migrations remove` before deploy or `Update-Database` to the previous migration after deploy. Data loss on rollback is limited to the two new tables.
- On a half-applied state (tables exist, code not yet deployed), the API is unaffected — the tables are simply unused. Safe.
- If `LocalFileStorage` is configured with a shared root, deleting the customers root would also affect tickets — document in `Program.cs` and add a comment on `AttachmentsOptions`.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** run `dotnet build` in `backend/`.
2. **Backend tests:** run `dotnet test` in `backend/CRM.Api.Tests/`. All new files must pass; existing ticket suites must remain green.
3. **Migration applies:** run `dotnet ef database update` against a dev PostgreSQL and confirm tables `TicketMessages`, `TicketAttachments` exist with expected indexes.
4. **Frontend runs:** `npm run dev` in `frontend/CRM.Web/`; open a ticket details page and exercise messages, attachments, history, escalate.
5. **Frontend tests:** `npm run test:unit` in `frontend/CRM.Web/`.
6. **Regression:** re-run `TicketsEndpointsTests.cs`, `TicketsAssignmentEndpointsTests.cs`, `TicketsHistoryEndpointsTests.cs`, `TicketsStatusEndpointsTests.cs`, `TicketsPriorityEndpointsTests.cs`.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Agents can post messages on a ticket, flag them internal vs public, and see them newest-first.
- [ ] Agents can upload, list, download, and delete ticket attachments with the same size/mime rules as customer attachments.
- [ ] The ticket details view shows a unified history timeline including status, assignment, priority, message, attachment, and escalation events.
- [ ] Managers/Admins can escalate a non-terminal, non-max-priority ticket with a required reason; priority bumps by one step and history records `Escalated`.
- [ ] Escalation is denied (403) for non-elevated roles and (400) for terminal or max-priority tickets.
- [ ] New backend and frontend tests are added and pass; no existing ticket test regresses.
- [ ] EF Core migration `AddTicketMessagesAttachments` is committed and applies cleanly forward and backward.
- [ ] No duplication of assignment/status/priority/authorization/history logic already delivered by CRM-94/95.
